title: Exome analysis of 22319 individuals links extremely rare copy-number variants and 22q11.21 dosage to Alzheimer risk.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no Zenodo/Dryad hits. The only NCBI PMC link (PMC13579704) resolved to an unrelated Brain Communications review, not this paper.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the cohort (22,319 exomes: 4,150 EOAD, 8,519 LOAD, 9,650 controls; 33,977 cases and 362,322 controls in replication) comes from the abstract alone. That the exomes sit in controlled-access repositories (ADES-FR consortium data, ADSP via dbGaP/NIAGADS, UK Biobank-scale replication) is inferred from the cohort type and was not confirmed in a data statement.

a1_downloadable.note: Individual-level human exome CNV calls (CNV = copy-number variant, a deleted or duplicated stretch of DNA) from AD (Alzheimer disease) case-control cohorts; no open deposit found. This kind of data normally needs a dbGaP/NIAGADS/UK Biobank access application, which counts as a fail. Not verified in files, since none were reachable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked: no files. Case/control status would be a phenotype column in controlled-access data only.

a5_enough_rows.note: Abstract claims 22,319 individuals, but no row count was verified.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked: clinical diagnosis labels, but no files available.

honest_claim_h3: Not reached: data is not openly downloadable.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's rare gene deletions and duplications to predict whether they develop early-onset or late-onset Alzheimer disease.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-person rare copy-number variant calls (deleted or duplicated gene regions) from exome sequencing; about 22,319 people per the abstract, unverified.
plain_idea.predict: Alzheimer case status (early-onset, late-onset, or unaffected), taken from clinical diagnosis in the source cohorts.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Could rank which rare deletions or duplications matter for Alzheimer risk, but the paper's burden tests already do this, and the data is behind access controls.

ml_idea: Case/control classifier from gene-level CNV dosage. Not pursued: the individual-level data is controlled access.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find the paper's data availability statement and confirm whether any per-individual CNV table is openly deposited; most likely it is not.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: human Alzheimer exome cohorts with no open deposit found, so individual-level data almost certainly needs a controlled-access application (dbGaP/NIAGADS/UK Biobank type). The paper isn't open access, and only summary association statistics would be public.
